analysis: Reviewed the base-side text of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 1-2004). The PR modifies only this test fixture: it adds an additional_context {enable_thinking:false} member to a template_input and regenerates token counts, chain hashes and token IDs (prompt_token_count 803->767, block boundaries dropped from three to two). The patch excerpt is truncated, and the changed base ranges (about 3024+, 3844, 43813, ...) fall outside the supplied base text, so the actual changed lines were not viewable. No code, authorization, key, attestation or encryption logic changes. The fixtures contain only synthetic prompts, with no secrets or real consumer data. Security relevance is indirect: the prompt contract and chain hashes feed cache routing and prefix-cache keying (T-041, TB-007). The token and hash changes depend on the template/renderer behavior change, which is not in the supplied evidence. Open integration question: whether the renderer change that sets additional_context.enable_thinking=false changes cache-scope or prompt_contract_id derivation, since prompt_contract_id stays the same (8171fec...) while token IDs and chain hashes change. If the contract ID is meant to cover renderer behavior, a stale ID could allow cross-contract cache reuse. I cannot confirm that from the supplied evidence, so I record it here and raise no finding. TB-002 and TB-009 were examined; the fixture change does not touch the coordinator-provider boundary or attestation.
